elements.element: Vendor has an express duty to defend Customer and its affiliates.
elements.evidence: Inserted 9(c) says only "HDI shall indemnify the Company against any third-party claim"; there is no "defend" (or "hold harmless") obligation and no reference to affiliates. To meet this element the operative text must read "shall defend, indemnify and hold harmless the Company and its affiliates".

elements.element: Vendor indemnifies Customer and its affiliates against third-party claims.
elements.evidence: The indemnity runs only to "the Company"; affiliates are not named as indemnified parties anywhere in 9(c).

elements.element: Vendor indemnity covers claims that Services or Deliverables infringe intellectual property rights.
elements.evidence: "any third-party claim alleging that the Site or the services provided by HDI under this Agreement infringe or misappropriate any intellectual property right" — the Site is the deliverable and the services are covered.

elements.element: Vendor indemnity covers Vendor's breach of applicable law.
elements.evidence: 9(c) is limited to IP infringement/misappropriation claims; no limb for HDI's breach of applicable law was inserted.

elements.element: Vendor indemnity covers a data breach caused by Vendor.
elements.evidence: No unauthorised-access/disclosure-of-Company-data limb appears in the inserted paragraph.

elements.element: Vendor indemnity covers Vendor's gross negligence and wilful misconduct.
elements.evidence: No gross negligence or wilful misconduct trigger in 9(c); the only trigger is the IP allegation.

elements.element: The indemnification procedure requires notice of a claim.
elements.evidence: 9(c) contains no notice mechanic; the margin comment expressly defers notice/control/cooperation, and a promise in the comment does not count.

elements.element: The indemnification procedure allocates control of the defence.
elements.evidence: No allocation of defence control (or settlement consent) in the inserted operative language.

elements.element: The indemnification procedure requires reasonable cooperation.
Customer indemnity is limited to Customer-provided content and Customer's breach of law.
elements.evidence: Conditional element: the Agreement contains no Company indemnity at all (only the Section 7.2 advertising-content covenant), and the redline does not add one, so no Company indemnity exceeds the permitted narrow scope.

elements.element: Vendor indemnifies Customer against third-party intellectual-property claims.
elements.evidence: "HDI shall indemnify the Company against any third-party claim alleging that the Site or the services provided by HDI under this Agreement infringe or misappropriate any intellectual property right".

elements.element: The IP indemnity may exclude infringement caused by Customer modifications.
elements.evidence: "except to the extent the claim arises from modifications made by the Company" — a permitted customary exclusion.

elements.element: The IP indemnity may exclude infringement caused by Customer combinations.
elements.evidence: "combination of the Site with items not supplied by HDI" — permitted combination exclusion.

elements.element: The IP indemnity may exclude infringement caused by Customer specifications.
elements.evidence: "or the Company's specifications" — permitted specification exclusion.

elements.element: Vendor must procure continued use, modify, or replace the infringing item.
elements.evidence: "HDI shall procure for the Company the right to continue using the affected item, or modify or replace it so that it is non-infringing" — stated as a mandatory HDI obligation.

elements.element: Vendor must refund applicable fees if procure, modify, or replace remedies are unavailable.
elements.evidence: "if none of those remedies is reasonably available, HDI shall refund the fees paid by the Company for the affected item".

elements.element: Vendor's indemnity is subject to a super-cap of three times annual fees.
elements.evidence: "HDI's total liability under this Section 9(c) shall not exceed three (3) times the fees paid or payable by the Company under this Agreement in the twelve (12) months preceding the claim" — 3× a twelve-month fee base, scoped to the indemnity only.

reasons: The fallback checklist is complete: every one of the seven fallback elements is present in operative language in the inserted Section 9(c), with no element left to the margin comment.

The preferred level fails on six elements — no duty to defend, no affiliate coverage, and no breach-of-law, data-breach or gross negligence/wilful misconduct limbs, plus no notice/control/cooperation procedure. To reach preferred, redraft the opening as "HDI shall defend, indemnify and hold harmless the Company and its affiliates ... to the extent arising out of (a) ... (b) HDI's breach of applicable law; (c) any unauthorised access to or disclosure of Company data caused by HDI; or (d) HDI's gross negligence or wilful misconduct", and add a notice/defence-control/cooperation sentence.

Minimality holds: Sections 9(a) and 9(b) are retained verbatim, nothing outside the checklist was deleted or paraphrased, and the insertion carries no extras (no survival tail, no separate attorneys'-fees or damages-category expansion, no procedure beyond the elements). The concise new paragraph is acceptable for a missing clause even though all its words are new.

Intent is preserved: the paragraph is lettered "(c)" so the cap's internal cross-reference to Section 9(c) resolves, it introduces no undefined terms (Site, Company, HDI are all defined), and it does not contradict the retained warranty or Globix language.

Note for the drafter (not a defect against the checklist): the 3× cap is drafted as a ceiling on HDI's liability under 9(c) where the Agreement previously had none, so confirm it is expressed as a super-cap sitting above any general limitation rather than as a new stand-alone limit on our recovery.
